scope: Lean-to-KB expository coverage review: definitions and important intermediate results
authority: Fixed Lean source is primary; no Lean execution or new correctness audit
method: Enumerate all named declarations in the preserved 34-module source using the existing Python index.
Compare the definition/structure inventory and theorem families with existing node statements, proofs, core declaration mappings, and chapter guides.
Use lexical reference frequency only to prioritize candidates; it is neither proof dependency nor mathematical importance.
Read the selected source statements, surrounding assumptions, and proof bodies before writing additions.
Keep reusable concepts and important results as distinct entries; retain coordinate, transport, instance, and simplification helpers in their mathematical proofs.
Generate source locations, URLs, term occurrences, and the declaration inventory in Python.
limits: A missing direct core-declaration mapping is not automatically an exposition gap. A broader proof can explain a helper without declaring it as a separate node.
The inventory records every indexed declaration; semantic review is at concept/theorem-family level and detailed for the additions. It is not an individual prose-proof audit of all 2991 declarations.
Build checks and source hashes validate document structure and provenance; they do not certify mathematical or pedagogical completeness.

module_reviews.assessment: Added primitive projectors, split-summand recognition, and adjoint primitivity. The broader boundary-pairing proof already explains the adjoint descent and range-duality constructions.

Added the simultaneous free-stalk/edge-kernel theorem, coefficient transport, word characters, and the two head-kernel maps within the detailed character proof. This module previously had no directly indexed core declaration in a KB entry.
Added the lower/upper simple envelopes and the lifting theorem, including its edge-transport argument. Existing subword and uniqueness entries cover the other principal results.

The lower-half construction, defect, strict degree bound, reciprocity, and canonical uniqueness are already distinct entries. Evaluation and interval-endpoint helper lemmas remain within those arguments.
Added ungraded local models and the word R-convolution theorem. Existing entries retain boundary reciprocity, simultaneous model character decomposition, and conditional character identification.
Elementary transfers, positivity, injectivity, endpoint rigidity, and reciprocal-polynomial rigidity are already represented. The ideal-state helper belongs to the existing schedule-comparison proof.
Strong exchange is already a theorem entry. The signed reflection-action record is now explained as the intermediate sign-tracking construction in the inversion-count proof.

Added angular plane-basis data. Pair projections and Frobenius coordinates were already defined; model-character summation and induced dihedral geometry are covered in their broader mathematical entries.
The dihedral KL-one theorem and square-parameter KL normalization are already represented. Alternating-word calculations remain inside the dihedral proof.
The induced-model interpolation theorem and transported later-edge count are already separate entries. Rank-one structure sheaves now have an independent definition.

The geometric Dyer proof already explains adapted-order rotation and path recurrences, and the relative-dihedral transport entry explains the interval maps. The angular plane basis is now separately defined.
